intro: Tests object pronouns (me, him, etc.), possessive adjectives (my, his, etc.), and subject pronouns (I, he, etc.)

items.q: This is my brother. I love ___.
items.why: Object pronoun needed after verb love.

items.q: ___ is a student. She studies every day.
items.why: Subject pronoun needed at start of sentence.

items.q: Can you help ___? I don't understand the question.
items.why: Object pronoun needed after verb help.

items.q: This is ___ dog. His name is Max.
items.why: Possessive adjective needed before a noun.

items.q: We like the teacher. ___ explains very clearly.
items.why: Subject pronoun needed as subject of the sentence.

parts.title: Complete the sentences with the correct form.

items.why: Object pronoun replaces subject pronoun after a verb.
Possessive adjective shows the bag belongs to her.

items.post: are my friends. I see them every day.
items.why: Subject pronoun needed as the subject of the sentence.
Possessive adjective needed before the noun name.
Object pronoun needed after preposition to.

parts.title: Find and correct the mistake in each sentence.

items.sentence: I see she every morning at the bus stop.
items.corrected: I see her every morning at the bus stop.
items.why: Object pronoun her needed after verb, not subject pronoun she.

items.sentence: This is my sister. Her is very funny.
items.corrected: This is my sister. She is very funny.
items.why: Subject pronoun she needed as subject, not possessive adjective her.

items.sentence: Can you give the book to I?
items.corrected: Can you give the book to me?
items.why: Object pronoun me needed after preposition, not subject pronoun I.

parts.title: Write your own sentences.
parts.pointsLabel: 2 points: 1 for correct form, 1 for meaning and use

items.prompt: Write one sentence about something that belongs to you, for example a book, a bag, or a phone.
items.criteria: Accept any sentence using a possessive adjective correctly, e.g. my, your, his, her.
items.example: My bag is on the table.

items.prompt: Write one sentence about a friend or family member. Say what you do with them or for them.
items.criteria: Accept any sentence using an object pronoun correctly, e.g. me, him, her, us, them.
